mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day forward returns are positive despite rising FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate crosses above 4.5%, signaling aggressive monetary tightening, it reduces equity valuations and triggers negative S&P 500 returns within the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5%, or the rate movement is temporary and reverses within weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% triggers investor risk aversion, reducing equity demand and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur when UNRATE crosses above 4.0%, or the unemployment rate decline is transitory.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and household spending (HOUST) signals robust demand, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Negative returns persist despite rising GDPC1 and HOUST, or one proxy lags the other.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates stronger business activity, enhancing corporate earnings and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite rising INDPRO, or supply factors like inventory levels dominate.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-recession recovery regime, rising industrial production (INDPRO) amplifies corporate earnings growth, leading to significantly higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Returns fail to rise in the post-recession regime despite INDPRO growth, or the regime is not actively transitioning.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals tight labor markets, boosting corporate profits and equity values, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Negative returns occur despite falling UNRATE, or inflationary pressures offset gains.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate below 1.0% signals recessionary pressures, reducing consumer and business spending, and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive returns occur when GDPC1 exceeds 1.0%, or the GDP growth is temporary and recovers quickly.
